chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to bow (ruku'), and he said, 'He must repeat (the prayer).'

All these narrations are understood to refer to forgetting the bowing in the first two rak'ahs, for in that case he must restart the prayer upon remembering. As for if the forgetting was in the last two rak'ahs and he remembered while still in the prayer, he should discard the two prostrations of the rak'ah in which he forgot the bowing and complete the prayer. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.رُكُوع: Bow (the second position in Islamic prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person forgets to bow (ruku') during Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between restarting the prayer (*i'adah*) versus completing it (*tamm*) based on whether the error occurred in the first or last two rak'ahs. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that forgetting a pillar in the initial half of the prayer necessitates a full restart, whereas errors in the latter half are corrected by discarding the specific rak'ah and continuing. The text highlights the precision required in ritual prayer, ensuring the validity of the worshipper's connection with the Divine through correct physical and spiritual posture.
